stories.title: FRP, Woodfield Begin Work on Expansive Estero Development
stories.excerpt: FRP Development Corp, in partnership with Woodfield Development, has started construction on the first phase of its Coconut Road mixed-use development in the Village of Estero, Florida. At 23281 Lyden Drive, across from Coconut Point, the development is planned to include approximately 600 apartment homes, 80,000 square feet of retail space, 20,000 square feet of office space and a boutique 190-room hotel. It’s to be designed by Dover Kohl & Partners. Estero is south of Fort Myers. The first phase will include approximately 296 apartment homes in a mix of three- and four-story residential buildings, together with 30,000 square feet of retail space. Initial residential units are anticipated to deliver in the third quarter of 2027. The developers secured an $81.5 million construction loan from Santander Bank to support construction of the project. Construction of the first phase is being led by general contractor Brooks & Freund, in collaboration with Humphreys & Partners Architects and interior design firm ID & Design International. The post FRP, Woodfield Begin Work on Expansive Estero Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: FRP & Woodfield broke ground on 296-unit Phase 1, Estero FL mixed-use; $81.5M Santander loan.
First residential units deliver Q3 2027; full project planned for ~600 apartments plus retail/hotel.
Project across from Coconut Point anchors south Fort Myers submarket supply pipeline.
stories.summary: FRP Development and Woodfield Development have begun construction on Phase 1 of Coconut Road in Estero, Florida, a mixed-use development ultimately planned for approximately 600 apartment homes, 80,000 sq ft of retail, 20,000 sq ft of office, and a 190-room boutique hotel. Phase 1 delivers 296 units with 30,000 sq ft of retail, with first resident move-ins anticipated in Q3 2027. Santander Bank provided an $81.5 million construction loan to fund the project.
stories.impact: New supply in the rapidly growing Estero/South Fort Myers corridor signals developer confidence in Southwest Florida demand but will add competitive pressure on existing Class A communities in the submarket. Delivery window Q3 2027 places this in mid-cycle absorption phase; monitor lease-up velocity and rent trajectory against Class A comps to gauge market health and feasibility of follow-on phases.

stories.title: Alpharetta Mall May Convert to Mixed-Use Entertainment Center
stories.excerpt: The North Point Mall may be transformed into a sports-adjacent, mixed-use entertainment center. In a major move for professional sports in Georgia, the Alpharetta City Council voted to approve a vision to transform North Point Mall into a sports-adjacent, mixed-use entertainment district. Its all contingent on the NHL awarding a franchise team to the North Point site. The proposal, led by Jamestown on behalf of site owner New York Life and in partnership with Machete Group, includes a 20,000-seat NHL-ready arena, a 4,000-seat music hall and performing arts center, a 2,000-seat community hockey rink, a 1,100-seat movie theater, a 35,000-square-foot hotel conference center, and up to 650 rooms across two hotel buildings. The project also includes approximately 565,000 square feet of retail and dining, 750,000 square feet of office, 1,385 for-rent multifamily units, and more than 20 acres of publicly accessible parks, plazas and multi-use trails. The redevelopment is expected to be completed in phases, with various components opening on a rolling basis. The post Alpharetta Mall May Convert to Mixed-Use Entertainment Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alpharetta City Council approved North Point Mall transformation to mixed-use sports district, contingent on NHL franchise.
Proposal includes 1,385 for-rent multifamily units, 565K SF retail, 750K SF office, subject to NHL award.
Jamestown & Machete Group leading redevelopment; phased delivery pending franchise decision.
stories.summary: Alpharetta City Council approved a vision led by Jamestown (on behalf of owner New York Life) and Machete Group to transform North Point Mall into a sports-anchored mixed-use entertainment district, contingent on an NHL franchise award to the site. The plan includes 1,385 for-rent multifamily units, 565,000 sq ft of retail/dining, 750,000 sq ft of office, two hotels (1,100 rooms total), and supporting sports/entertainment venues. The redevelopment will roll out in phases pending NHL approval.
stories.impact: Contingency on NHL franchise award creates execution risk and timing uncertainty for multifamily component. If awarded, the sports anchor will drive significant foot traffic and employment density in Alpharetta, likely supporting premium rent positioning and strong lease-up for the 1,385 units. The office component (750K SF) is outsized and may compete for capital; monitor whether multifamily gets accelerated or deprioritized based on sports timeline.

stories.title: Thompson Thrift Pursuing 319-Unit Powder Springs Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Thompson Thrift is moving ahead on Avira at Silver Comet Trail, a 319-unit multifamily community in the Atlanta suburb of Powder Springs. Construction is underway with resident move-ins expected to begin in October 2027. Located at the southeast corner of Highway 278 and Isley Stamper Road, the community will offer convenient access to downtown Powder Springs, major retail destinations, healthcare providers and employment centers throughout the Atlanta metropolitan area. Avira at Silver Comet Trail will feature a mix of one-, two- and three-bedroom apartment homes in three- and four-story buildings with private patio, balcony and yard options. Residents will enjoy a swimming pool, fitness center, courtyards, pickleball court, dog park and pet spa. Additional outdoor features will include a basketball court, grilling areas, coworking focus suites, billiards, shuffleboard, and other lifestyle-focused amenities. The development will be capitalized with equity from the Thompson Thrift 2026 Multifamily Development, LP. The post Thompson Thrift Pursuing 319-Unit Powder Springs Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Thompson Thrift underway on 319-unit Avira at Silver Comet Trail, Powder Springs GA; move-ins October 2027.
Mix of 1-, 2-, 3-bed units in 3-4 story buildings; equity from Thompson Thrift 2026 Multifamily Development, LP.
Located SE corner Highway 278 & Isley Stamper Road; targets Atlanta metro employment reach.
stories.summary: Thompson Thrift is constructing Avira at Silver Comet Trail, a 319-unit multifamily community in Powder Springs, Georgia (Atlanta suburb), with resident move-ins beginning October 2027. The project features a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units across three- and four-story buildings, with amenities including pool, fitness center, dog park, pickleball, basketball court, and coworking suites. The development is capitalized by equity from Thompson Thrift 2026 Multifamily Development, LP.
stories.impact: Powder Springs is an emerging suburban Atlanta growth node; this 319-unit delivery adds supply to a historically undersupplied exurban market. Positioning on Highway 278 captures commute-shed demand from employment centers north and east. Late 2027 delivery aligns with anticipated rate normalization; monitor competing supply in I-75 corridor (Marietta, Kennesaw) to assess absorption risk and rent growth sustainability.

stories.title: Carrier Eyeing Fort Worth for $433M Plant
stories.excerpt: HVAC giant Carrier is seeking the best deal from any one of three cities in a competition to build a $433.8 million manufacturing plant. Fort Worth is one of them. The city is proposing a seven-year tax abatement agreement valued at $10.9 million as an incentive for the company to bring the plant there. The city would also nominate the company for a Texas Enterprise Zone grant with an estimated value of $2.5 million. In return, the company would agree to a minimum capital investment of $433.8 million in a new plant by the end of 2028. Of that, $36 million would be spent on real property construction costs and $397.8 million on equipping the plant. The company would also pledge to spend 30% of construction costs with small businesses and provide a minimum of 495 jobs by the end of 2029 with a minimum average salary of $75,000. The proposed location is Alliance Westport 12, a 1.2 million-square-foot building.,being developed by Hillwood. Carrier plans to make a decision on the new manufacturing plant in the third quarter of this year. The post Carrier Eyeing Fort Worth for $433M Plant appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Carrier considering Fort Worth $433.8M HVAC manufacturing plant; City offering $10.9M tax abatement + $2.5M grant.
495+ minimum jobs at $75K+ salary by end 2029; $36M real property cost, $397.8M equipment.
Location: Alliance Westport 12 (1.2M SF) by Hillwood; decision Q3 2024.
stories.summary: HVAC giant Carrier is competing among three cities to build a $433.8 million manufacturing plant, with Fort Worth offering a 7-year tax abatement valued at $10.9 million plus a potential $2.5 million Texas Enterprise Zone grant. Carrier commits to minimum capital investment ($36M real property, $397.8M equipment), 495 jobs by end 2029 at average salary of $75,000, and 30% of construction spend with small businesses. The proposed site is Alliance Westport 12, a 1.2M sq ft building being developed by Hillwood. Decision expected Q3 2024.
stories.impact: Manufacturing job creation (495+ high-wage positions) in Fort Worth's Alliance submarket will drive near-term workforce migration and rental demand in the northwest corridor and surrounding submarkets. Tax incentives reduce development cost friction; if Carrier selects Fort Worth, anticipate increased multifamily pre-leasing activity and rent momentum in proximity to Alliance over next 18 months. Monitor competing bids and final decision timing as signal of Fort Worth's competitive labor and incentive positioning.

stories.title: Law Firm Nutter Expands to 11K SF at Durst’s 5 Grand Central East
stories.excerpt: Law firm Nutter is taking more office space at one of the Durst Organization’s buildings near Grand Central Terminal, Commercial Observer has learned. Nutter, which is based in Boston and provides personal and business legal services, has signed a deal to renew its existing 5,719 square feet on the 27th floor of Durst’s 5 Grand Central East — also known as 655 Third Avenue — and add another 5,719 square feet on the entire 25th floor, according to the landlord. The deal brings the law firm’s total footprint at the 30-story office tower to 11,438 square feet. “The Manhattan office leasing market is surging, especially for Class A spaces in transit-accessible locations such as Grand Central East,” Jody Durst, president of Durst, said in a statement. “Nutter’s decision to expand at 5 Grand Central East reflects the desirability of the area and Durst’s long-term investment in our buildings.” The length of the lease was not provided, but the asking rent was $80 per square foot, according to Durst. CBRE’s Michael Joyce and Trevor Larkin brokered the deal for Nutter, while Durst was repped in-house by Tom Bow, Ashlea Aaron, Bailey Caliban and Sayo Kamara. A spokesperson for CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Nutter, which was founded in 1879, has been a tenant in Durst’s office building between East 41st and East 42nd streets since 2022. Michael Scott, co-managing partner of Nutter, said in a statement that 5 Grand Central East is “the right location for our clients and our team as we grow.” In December, Durst rebranded two of its office buildings near Grand Central, turning 655 Third Avenue to 5 Grand Central East and renaming 733 Third Avenue as 11 Grand Central East. The rebranding reflected its “continued investment in the Grand Central submarket,” the firm said. bullets: Law firm Nutter expanded at Durst's 5 Grand Central East, Manhattan; +5,719 SF on 25th floor.

Office leasing strength near Grand Central Terminal reflects post-pandemic Manhattan recovery.
stories.summary: Boston-based law firm Nutter has expanded at the Durst Organization's 5 Grand Central East (655 Third Avenue) in Manhattan, renewing its existing 5,719 sq ft on the 27th floor and adding an additional 5,719 sq ft on the entire 25th floor, bringing total occupancy to 11,438 sq ft. The asking rent was $80 per sq ft. Durst highlighted strong Manhattan office demand in transit-accessible Class A locations near Grand Central Terminal.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Office leasing recovery in Midtown Manhattan signals increasing corporate confidence and in-office labor demand, which historically supports residential leasing in Manhattan's core rental markets. However, this is offset by office-to-residential conversion trends and limited new multifamily supply in the CBD; unlikely to materially affect multifamily development feasibility or capital allocation.

stories.title: Sheppard Takes 107K SF at In-Rel’s D.C. Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: One of the 50 highest-grossing law firms in the U.S. has signed an anchor lease at a planned Washington, D.C., trophy office redevelopment three years before its anticipated completion. Law firm Sheppard signed for 107,224 square feet at In-Rel Properties’ 2033 K Street NW, CBRE announced Tuesday. The firm, which has more than 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices, will move in after the building’s expected completion in July 2029. The brokerage did not disclose the value of the lease or the asking rent. In-Rel is expanding and updating the existing building, located along K Street near the intersection of D.C.’s Central Business District, West End and Dupont Circle. The developer will retain the property’s concrete structure while expanding it vertically and horizontally, including adding three floors and a penthouse. The renovations are another example of owners betting on Washington’s bifurcated office market, where distress coexists with a shortage of large, new trophy spaces, particularly for law firms and other high-end tenants. “We all know D.C. has plenty of office space, but what it doesn’t have is enough large-block, trophy-quality product that leading law firms like Sheppard demand,” In-Rel CEO Jackson Siegal said in a statement. Sheppard Chair Luca Salvi said the new office would provide a more modern and efficient workplace as the firm approaches its centennial and continues growing its Washington operation. CBRE’s Dimitri Hajimihalis, Emily Eppolito and Carroll Cavanagh represented In-Rel. Savills’ Gary Stein, David Lipson, Jon Glass and Owen Jaccard represented Sheppard. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Law firm Sheppard signed anchor lease for 107K SF at In-Rel's 2033 K Street NW, Washington D.C.
Tenant move-in July 2029; In-Rel redeveloping existing building with +3 floors and penthouse.
Top 50 U.S. law firm (1,200+ attorneys) leasing trophy office signals DC CBD recovery.
stories.summary: Law firm Sheppard, one of the 50 highest-grossing law firms in the U.S. with over 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices, has signed an anchor lease for 107,224 square feet at In-Rel Properties' 2033 K Street NW in Washington, D.C. Move-in is expected after the building's completion in July 2029. In-Rel is vertically and horizontally expanding the existing structure, adding three floors and a penthouse while retaining the concrete core.
stories.impact: Trophy office leasing 3+ years ahead of completion in a bifurcated D.C. market signals developer confidence in CBD recovery and large-tenant demand for Class A space. This de-risks the K Street redevelopment and may attract follow-on office and mixed-use development nearby. Secondary effect: office projects often include residential components; monitor In-Rel and similar D.C. developers for multifamily add-ons. Anchor tenant commitment may support higher office valuations and potentially cross-subsidize residential components in future mixed-use projects.

stories.title: Eliot Spitzer Gains State Approval to Redevelop 985 Fifth Avenue After Legal Bout
stories.excerpt: Former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer will finally get to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue after suing the state to obtain approval. Spitzer claimed that the state’s Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) was delaying the approval of an application to not renew rent-stabilized leases in the building, a necessary step before the property could be redeveloped. Spitzer ultimately won the state’s blessing. The two-year request to end the rent-stabilized leases on the property followed approval from the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 2023 to take a wrecking ball to the 25-story rental property and construct luxury condominiums in its place. Spitzer alleged potential misconduct in the lawsuit, reported by The Real Deal. Spitzer could not be reached for comment. HCR, now under the administration of Gov. Kathy Hochul, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Spitzer’s Spitzer Enterprises has been advancing on other aspects of the project despite the delay, unveiling designs by SLCE Architects for the property in November 2025 which would yield 25 condo units, according to New York YIMBY. The former governor, who resigned in 2008 during a prostitution scandal, has owned the property since at least 2018 after buying seven residential buildings in the city, including 800 Fifth Avenue, with a total of 1.5 million square feet. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Former NY Gov. Spitzer won court approval to demolish rent-stabilized 985 Fifth Avenue, NYC.
Two-year rent-stabilization lease non-renewal request; LPC approved wrecking ball in 2023; now HCR approval secured.
Redevelopment planned as luxury condominiums; SLCE Architects design unveiled.
stories.summary: Former New York Governor Eliot Spitzer has obtained state approval from the Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) to proceed with demolishing the 25-story rent-stabilized residential building at 985 Fifth Avenue after a lawsuit over delayed approval. The New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission had already approved demolition in 2023. Spitzer's plan is to construct luxury condominiums on the site, with designs by SLCE Architects already unveiled.
stories.impact: For-sale condo conversion, not multifamily rental; minimal direct impact on apartment REIT or development operations. However, removal of rent-stabilized stock signals ongoing deregulation pressure and potential for for-sale conversions in other Manhattan Class A locations. This may compete for Manhattan luxury residential capital and contractor bandwidth, affecting multifamily development timelines and cost. Monitor if other owners follow with rent-stabilized demolition/condo conversions—could fragment high-end Manhattan rental market.

stories.title: OCVibe Adds Five Dining Concepts to $5B SoCal District
stories.excerpt: The Samueli family has added five more dining concepts to the 50,000-square-foot market hall set to open next year as part of the $5 billion mixed-use development called OCVibe surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, Calif. Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll and Gelato Paradiso are the five new food options, adding Mexican, Filipino, Northern Chinese and Italian menus to the 21-kitchen market hall named Katella Commons. They join a growing roster at OCVibe, which earlier added concepts from chefs behind Amiga Amore, Burritos La Palma, Evil Cooks, Manaao Thai Comfort Food and Darkroom Restaurant and Wine Bar. Beloved Los Angeles chef Roy Choi is also bringing his Best Friend restaurant to the district. OCVibe did not disclose the values of the leases or the sizes of each space. Sources familiar with the development told Commercial Observer that OCVibe is fronting the initial investment, which averages around $300,000 per stall, as well as providing ongoing operational supports. “We wanted to approach this differently than a traditional landlord-tenant relationship,” OCVibe Senior Vice President Scott Frick said in a statement shared with CO. “Independent chefs are often asked to take on significant financial and operational risk before they ever serve their first meal. And unfortunately, many restaurants fail because of the significant upfront investment required of them.” Indeed, Frick recently told Commercial Observer that the Samueli family’s ownership structure has allowed the project to take a hands-on approach to restaurant leasing. Ownership is funding Katella Commons down to the kitchen equipment, allowing tenants to avoid substantial upfront costs of fitting out the new spaces. “Any tenant that comes in doesn’t have to come in with capital to fit out the kitchen — basically bring in your own knives and we’ll turn on the menu boards,” Frick said. bullets: OCVibe (Samueli family) added 5 dining concepts to 50K SF Katella Commons food hall, Anaheim CA.
OCVibe is $5B mixed-use district anchored by Honda Center; developers fronting ~$300K/stall + ops support.

stories.summary: The Samueli family's OCVibe mixed-use development surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, California, has announced five additional dining concepts for the 50,000 sq ft Katella Commons market hall, set to open next year. New tenants include Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll, and Gelato Paradiso, joining previously announced chefs and concepts. OCVibe is providing initial build-out capital (averaging ~$300K per stall) and ongoing operational support for tenants.
stories.impact: OCVibe's $5B mixed-use scale and food-hall strategy signal strong demand capture and destination positioning. Food hall success typically drives foot traffic to adjacent residential; the 50K SF Katella Commons will anchor daytime/evening occupancy and support rental demand for future multifamily components. Samueli's willingness to front operator capex ($300K/stall) indicates confidence in volume and reduces tenant risk, a favorable signal for adjacent multifamily lease-up and rent stability. Monitor OCVibe's residential component delivery timing and pricing for Anaheim market validation.

stories.title: The New School Sells Loeb Hall Residence to Hawkins Way Capital for $52M
stories.excerpt: In its third acquisition of student housing in Manhattan this summer, Hawkins Way Capital has purchased a residence hall near Union Square for $51.5 million from the New School, according to city records made public Tuesday. Hawkins, using the entity 135 E 12th Owner, bought Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, directly from The New School, records show. Joshua Bird, managing director and general counsel at Hawkins, signed the deal for the buyer, while Loretta Ferrari, chief financial officer at the New School, signed for the seller. “We’ve long been looking for the right opportunity in this neighborhood, and this property represents an ideal addition to our portfolio,” Ross Walker, managing partner at Hawkins, said in a statement to Commercial Observer. “Its location, existing student housing infrastructure and flexibility put us in an ideal position to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country’s strongest urban student housing markets.” Loeb Hall was removed from the New School’s undergraduate housing options this year. The residence hall is four blocks east of the New School’s main University Center and administrative offices on Fifth Avenue, although the sprawling urban campus has numerous sites near Union Square. Francisco Pineda, executive vice president for business operations and chief operating officer at the New School, said the sale allows the institution to “redirect resources toward the priorities that matter most, while generating income that supports our long-term mission.” The former Loeb Hall will undergo renovations and be repositioned under Hawkins’ Found Study student housing platform, according to a spokesperson for Hawkins. A JLL team led by David Carlos brokered the recent sale. A spokesperson for JLL did not immediately respond to a request for comment. bullets: Hawkins Way Capital acquired 268-bed Loeb Hall student housing, New School, Manhattan for $51.5M.
Third Manhattan student housing acquisition by Hawkins this summer; 131-135 East 12th Street, Union Square.

stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital has purchased Loeb Hall, a 268-bed student residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street near Union Square in Manhattan, from The New School for $51.5 million. This is Hawkins Way's third student housing acquisition in Manhattan this summer. The buyer intends to leverage the property's existing student housing infrastructure and flexible footprint to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country's strongest urban student housing markets.
stories.impact: Student housing (institutional/purpose-built) is a distinct asset class but signals strong investor appetite for urban residential with steady cash flows and demographic tailwinds. Hawkins Way's three-acquisition summer spree in Manhattan reflects conviction in student housing NOI resilience and liquidity. Secondary effect on traditional multifamily: student housing can fragment young professional rental demand, but typically targets 18–25 age group; monitor displacement of traditional multifamily tenants if student housing inventory grows faster than underlying enrollment. Minimal near-term impact on Class A multifamily development pro formas, but signals capital competition and tenant demographic sorting in Manhattan CBD.
